questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the single most damaging common mistake?
options: Skipping the balancing-segment-value-to-legal-entity assignment, which silently breaks a clean trial balance per legal entity
Naming a segment something other than 'Company'
Using the Common Set for shared reference data
Enabling too many currencies
questions.explain: The lesson calls out the missing balancing-segment-value assignment as the most damaging mistake, since it silently breaks per-entity trial balance reporting and is often discovered late, under pressure.

questions.q: What problem can arise from writing cross-validation rules against individual values instead of hierarchies?
options: The rule becomes impossible to create at all
The rule requires ongoing manual maintenance every time a new value is added, instead of automatically extending through the hierarchy
It has no practical downside
It automatically disables the legal entity
questions.explain: As Lesson 23 and 24 covered, referencing a hierarchy node lets a rule automatically extend to new values; listing individual values instead requires manual updates.

questions.q: What two seemingly opposite chart of accounts mistakes does this lesson describe as having the same root cause?
options: Too many cost centers and too few natural accounts
Too many currencies and too few business units
Over-engineering (too many segments 'just in case') and under-planning (no reserved Future segment for predictable growth)
Too many legal entities and too few ledgers
questions.explain: Both over-engineering and under-planning trace back to skipping the deliberate design conversation from Lesson 5.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the root cause behind nearly every common enterprise structure mistake?
options: Using too many legal reporting units
Choosing the wrong conversion rate type
Oracle Fusion software bugs
Skipping deliberate design in favor of configuring quickly, under deadline pressure
questions.explain: The lesson ties nearly every mistake back to skipping the careful design step from Chapter 2 in favor of rushing into configuration.

questions.q: Which course does this lesson identify as the next step in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path?
options: Oracle Fusion Accounts Payable
Oracle Fusion General Ledger
Oracle Fusion Security
SQL for Oracle Financials
questions.explain: The course closes by pointing to Oracle Fusion General Ledger as the next course, where students put the enterprise structure foundation to work recording and reporting journal activity.
